settings.terminal.rtl.title: Hebrew / Arabic (RTL)
settings.terminal.rtl.profile.local.hint: Native Windows panes — cmd and PowerShell. The Windows console keeps right-to-left text visually ordered in its buffer and ConPTY passes that through, so these panes usually need "Full BiDi reorder".
settings.terminal.rtl.profile.remote.hin: Anything with a Linux shell behind it — SSH, and WSL too, since WSL is Linux with tmux and is local only geographically. These panes receive Hebrew in normal logical order, so they usually need "Auto per line".
settings.terminal.rtl.hint: How to display lines that contain right-to-left text. Switching the mode affects newly-opened panes immediately; existing panes update the write pipeline live but keep their original renderer.
settings.terminal.rtl.auto.label: Per-line auto (Termius-style)
settings.terminal.rtl.auto.desc: DOM renderer; each line gets dir="auto" and the browser picks direction by the first strong character. Best default for SSH prompts that occasionally print Hebrew.
settings.terminal.rtl.force.label: Full RTL (remote panes)
settings.terminal.rtl.force.desc: DOM renderer; EVERY line is forced dir="rtl" with no detection — no dominance vote, no table grouping. A shell that is unconditionally right-to-left. Latin words inside a line still read correctly. Built for remote (SSH/WSL) panes: full-screen TUIs such as tmux, vim or htop WILL look mirrored, because their layout is positional.
settings.terminal.rtl.bidi.label: Full BiDi reorder (legacy)
settings.terminal.rtl.bidi.desc: WebGL renderer + bidi-js logical→visual reorder. Faster paint, but rewrites the byte stream — editable lines may surprise.
settings.terminal.rtl.off.label: Off
settings.terminal.rtl.off.desc: WebGL renderer, no reorder. Hebrew bytes render left-to-right as written.
settings.terminal.use_ymux_tmux_config.h: Bundles a tmux.conf at ~/.ymux/tmux.conf so wheel scrolls the scrollback ring instead of shell history, 50k-line buffer, sane truecolour. Turn off to fall back to your own ~/.tmux.conf. Takes effect on next pane connect.
settings.sessions.visibility.label: tmux session picker scope
settings.sessions.visibility.hint: Which sessions the Connect picker lists when several machines share the same server user.
settings.sessions.visibility.shared: All sessions on the server (default) — including ones created from other machines
settings.sessions.visibility.local: Only sessions created from this machine
settings.terminal.auto_direction.label: Auto-direction per line
settings.terminal.auto_direction.hint: A line containing Hebrew/Arabic (including mixed) renders right-to-left; a pure-Latin line renders left-to-right. Applies to the "auto per line" mode.
Clears stale mouse-tracking that an app (vim/fzf/less) left on after an unclean exit — which shows up as \e[<..M escapes in the terminal. Also available any time via Ctrl+Alt+R.
settings.terminal.mirror_arrows_rtl.labe: Mirror arrow keys on RTL lines
settings.terminal.mirror_arrows_rtl.hint: On a Hebrew/Arabic line the physical Left/Right arrows move the opposite logical direction; this flips them to match what you see. Only active on RTL lines — English lines are unaffected.
settings.terminal.tui_owns_bidi.label: Claude Code writes Hebrew already reversed
settings.terminal.tui_owns_bidi.hint: Claude Code on Windows emits RTL in visual order — the letters arrive pre-reversed. With this on, ymux renders those bytes verbatim instead of reordering them a second time, and un-reverses them again on copy so a paste reads correctly. ON by default for local panes, off for remote ones, which do not do this.
settings.terminal.direction_policy.label: Weigh Hebrew against Latin per row (experimental)
settings.terminal.direction_policy.hint: On a TUI status bar, one Hebrew word in a row of Latin should not flip the whole row — the TUI already chose the column of every glyph. With this on, Hebrew takes a row unless Latin outnumbers it by more than 4 to 1. Off is the long-standing rule: any Hebrew takes the row.
settings.autoConnect.label: Auto-connect on workspace select
settings.autoConnect.hint: When enabled, switching to an SSH workspace establishes a background connection so tmux sessions and your files are immediately visible. Disable to defer the connection until a terminal pane is opened.
settings.restoreSessions.label: Restore SSH sessions on startup
settings.restoreSessions.hint: When enabled, opening YMUX re-attaches the active workspace's SSH panes to the tmux sessions they were on when it closed. A pane is only re-attached after the server confirms its session is still alive — if it is gone, the pane keeps its Connect button. Costs one SSH handshake per restored pane at startup, and re-runs the workspace's setup command on each.
settings.fmRememberPath.label: File manager reopens at the last directory
settings.fmRememberPath.hint: When enabled, each column of the file manager reopens where you left it, remembered per workspace. When disabled, both columns always open at your home directory.

insights.cc.copy_intro: Below is a report of my Claude Code usage, read from its own transcripts by ymux. Tell me where it actually went: which projects, models and sessions dominated, whether the cache is working or being invalidated, how much came from subagents, and what I could change to get the same work for less. Note that the cost column is an API-list-price estimate, not a bill.
insights.cc.empty: No Claude Code usage in this range ({files} transcript file(s) scanned).
insights.cc.old_daemon: This server runs an Insights daemon from before the usage endpoint. Reinstall it from Settings → Add-ons to update.
insights.cc.estimate_note: Cost is an ESTIMATE, not a bill — a subscription is not billed per token. These are API list prices (table as of {asOf}) applied to real token counts: right for comparing where usage went, wrong for predicting a charge. Rows marked “~” mix several models and use a token-weighted blended rate.
insights.cc.unpriced: One or more models in this range have no published price, so their tokens are counted but not costed. The total is therefore a floor, not the whole figure.
insights.an.copy_hint: Copy this range as plain text — paste it into Claude and ask what happened. Machine metrics only.
insights.an.copy_intro: Below is a metrics report from my Linux server, collected by ymux. Tell me what actually happened over this window: how loaded the machine was, anything that spiked or is trending the wrong way, whether a disk is on course to fill up, and whether any container looks unhealthy. Point at the specific timestamps and numbers you are reasoning from. If something in here is too thin to support a conclusion, say so instead of guessing.
insights.an.empty: No history for this range yet. The daemon samples every 5s and keeps 7 days — check back in a few minutes.
insights.an.old_daemon: This server runs an Insights daemon from before the Analytics endpoint. Reinstall it from Settings → Add-ons to update.
